title: A Texas contract to sell real estate must be in a signed writing
rule: A contract for the sale of real estate is unenforceable unless it, or a memorandum of it, is in writing and signed by the person to be charged or someone lawfully authorized to sign for that person. The rule also covers real estate leases longer than one year and agreements not to be performed within a year. Separately, a Texas suit to recover a commission on a real estate sale or purchase needs a writing signed by the party sued.

citation.authority: Tex. Bus. & Com. Code 26.01(a) and (b)(4)-(6); Tex. Occ. Code 1101.806(c)
